notes: M.S. thesis (75 pp.), text extracted with pymupdf; figures not visible. Two methods: CKD (Tables 4.2-4.4) and DKD (Tables 4.5-4.7). All accuracies are averages over all E_T+S epochs (not final-epoch), for DKD further averaged over K runs; the paper never says whether +- is a standard deviation or what it is taken over. Times have no unit; teacher/student times are averaged over E_T+S epochs, distilled over E_S epochs (Sec. 4.2); figure times are normalised by dataset size. KD hyper-parameters (tau, alpha, z, delta) are stored as free text in tm_config.extra. delta in Table 4.2 is marked delta* and applies to TM_PCD only. Paper inconsistency: Sec. 3.2.1 says 'We find an optimal value at z = 0.2' but Table 4.5 uses z = 0.3 for MNIST and KMNIST. How z, delta (Sec. 4.2: 'chosen to find the best compromise between accuracy and speed') and the other hyper-parameters were chosen is not said and no validation set is mentioned, so selection_on_test is not_reported. Table 4.1 labels the feature count |L| (784 / 5000) although Eq. 1.4 defines |L| = 2n literals; stored as n_boolean_features, n_literals left not_reported. CKD distilled models take zeta x |C_T| teacher clause bits as input (Eq. 3.2), not the raw 784/5000 bits. EMNIST: 26 letter classes, 124,800/20,800 (the Letters split; the paper just says EMNIST). Not in the record (omissions, not errors): the DKD time columns carry +- values (e.g. MNIST T_T 0.37 +- 0.01, Table 4.7) while the record's time rows have std_or_range null; Table 4.3 (CKD training results) and the training times of Table 4.6 are not in the record. Record values checked against Tables 4.4, 4.6, 4.7: no disagreements.
